passage:
Monday. Ira, Aadhya's partner, sat on the edge of the bed after dinner and said, in a small voice, "When I was ten my father left, and for years I thought it was because of something I did." Aadhya felt honoured and a bit lost. There was no answer to fix that. Aadhya just took Ira's hand and said, "Thank you for telling me. I'm listening."

Wednesday. Over the phone, Aadhya's sister asked what was wrong. Aadhya almost told her, then said, "Something private. It isn't mine to share."

Saturday. On the walk home Ira said, "I've never said that to anyone. It felt lighter after." Then Ira started to tell the next part, a little at a time, and Aadhya kept listening.

qa.q: How old was Ira when Ira's father left?
How did Aadhya feel when Ira confided, and what did Aadhya do?
qa.a: Aadhya felt honoured and a bit lost, and took Ira's hand and said, "Thank you for telling me. I'm listening," without trying to fix anything.

qa.q: Why did Aadhya tell the sister "It isn't mine to share"?
qa.a: Aadhya understood that keeping Ira's confidence is what makes further openness safe, so it wasn't something to pass on even to a close relative.

qa.q: How might Ira have felt when saying it out loud for the first time?
qa.a: Ira probably felt exposed and hopeful. Ira said it felt lighter afterwards and went on to tell more, which suggests Aadhya's listening felt safe.

grounding: Shows a partner confiding something painful, the protagonist feeling honoured and unsure, listening without fixing or judging and keeping the confidence, so more openness follows.

passage:
Saturday, very late

Arohi told me tonight about her father. How he drank. How she used to hide under the bed with her little brother when he came home. She's never told anyone except her brother. She spoke for an hour, staring at the ceiling.

I'm Jagdish, and I felt honoured that she trusted me. Also completely lost. I wanted to say something wise. I wanted to fix it, to say, "But he's changed now, na?" I didn't. I just held her hand and listened. When she cried, I let her.

At the end she said, "You won't tell your mother, will you?"

I said, "Never. This is yours."

Tomorrow Amma will ask why Arohi looked tired at lunch. I'll say she didn't sleep well. That's all. If Arohi ever wants to tell her more, that's her choice.

I think the most important thing I did tonight was not speak.

qa.q: Where did Arohi hide as a child?
qa.a: Arohi hid under the bed with her little brother.

qa.q: What was Jagdish feeling while Arohi spoke?
qa.a: Jagdish felt honoured to be trusted and also lost, unsure what to say and tempted to fix it.

qa.q: What did Jagdish do that made further openness safe?
qa.a: Jagdish listened without fixing or judging, let Arohi cry, and promised to keep it from Jagdish's own mother.

qa.q: How might Arohi feel after Jagdish promised not to tell his mother?
qa.a: Arohi would likely feel safe and relieved, trusting that her pain stays hers to share.

grounding: The diary shows a young spouse honoured and unsure after a partner confides something painful, listening without fixing and keeping the confidence.

Chandrika: two years together and there's something I've never told you. or anyone
Pallavi: of course
Chandrika: in college I had panic attacks. bad ones. I dropped a semester because of them
Chandrika: my parents still think I took a break to travel
Pallavi: thank you for trusting me with that
Chandrika: you're not going to tell me what to do?
Pallavi: no. I just want to hear it. how was it for you?
Chandrika: lonely. I thought I was broken
Pallavi: that sounds so hard. I'm glad you told me
Chandrika: please don't tell your mum. she already asks too many questions
Pallavi: I won't. this is yours to share, not mine

On Sunday, at lunch, Pallavi's mother asked why Chandrika had left college for a semester. Pallavi said, "That's Chandrika's story, Ma," and passed the rice.

qa.q: Why did Chandrika drop a semester?
qa.a: Chandrika dropped a semester because of panic attacks.

qa.q: What was Pallavi feeling when Chandrika confided?
qa.a: Pallavi felt honoured to be trusted and caring, choosing to listen rather than fix.

qa.q: How did Pallavi make it safe for Chandrika to open up further?
qa.a: Pallavi listened without advice or judgement and kept the confidence at Sunday lunch, saying it was Chandrika's story.

qa.q: How might Chandrika feel when Pallavi protected the story at lunch?
qa.a: Chandrika would likely feel relieved and more trusting, knowing the private pain was safe.

grounding: The chat shows a young person whose partner confides something painful, listening without fixing and keeping the confidence so further openness is safe.
